cover.label: PEPSICO vs COCA-COLA
cover.headline: Pepsi sells twice as much as Coke. {Coke still earns more.}

slides.label: ROUND 1: SALES
slides.headline: Pepsi wins on {sales.} By a lot.
slides.body: Almost *double.* So Pepsi must be the bigger money machine, right? *Not so fast.*

slides.label: ROUND 2: PROFIT
slides.headline: Half the sales. {More profit.}
slides.source: Reported (GAAP) operating income, FY2025, per company filings

slides.label: WHY #1: COKE
slides.headline: Coke sells the {secret formula,} not the trucks.
slides.body: Coca-Cola mostly makes *concentrate and syrup* and sells it to *bottling partners,* who fill, ship and stock the shelves. Coke keeps the *high-margin* part and leaves the heavy lifting to others.

slides.label: WHY #2: PEPSI
slides.headline: Pepsi is a {snack empire} too.
slides.body: PepsiCo also owns *Frito-Lay* (Lay's, Doritos, Cheetos), *Quaker* and *Gatorade,* and runs much of its own *bottling and delivery.* That adds a lot of *sales,* but thinner margins.

slides.label: THE FINE PRINT
slides.headline: One-offs {skew} the gap.
slides.body: Pepsi's reported profit took a *$2 billion impairment* (mostly its Rockstar brand). Adjusted, PepsiCo's core operating profit was *$14.9 billion,* about *16%* of sales. Coke's adjusted margin: *31%.* Coke's still about *double.*

last.headline: Sales is vanity. {Margin} is sanity.
last.body: The company that makes less can still keep more. Which model would you rather own: Coke's formula or Pepsi's empire? Team Coke or team Pepsi?
